claim.claim-text: 1. A computer implemented method of assessing visual function of a user, comprising:
2. The computer implemented method as claimed in claim 1, further comprising presenting the optokinetic stimulus (S13) as a moving image of stripes, bars or checkerboards.

3. The computer implemented method as claimed in claim 1, further comprising presenting the optokinetic stimulus in varying directions on the display or further comprising presenting the optokinetic stimulus in a consistent direction on the display and presenting instructions to the user to hold the display in a desired orientation .
4. The computer implemented method as claimed in claim 1, further comprising presenting the optokinetic stimulus (S13) with varying width and spacing.

5. The computer implemented method as claimed in claim 1, further comprising calibrating (S1) a processor (12) of the handheld digital device (10) by capturing an image of eye structures, facial structures or both while including an object of known size in the captured image and/or further comprising determining a size of the eye structures (26), facial structures (24) or both relative to the object of known size (30) in the captured image and/or further comprising measuring the working distance (22) directly or on the basis of comparison to the object of known size (30) and/or further comprising measuring the working distance (22) while the optokinetic stimulus is viewed.

6. The computer implemented method as claimed in claim 1, further comprising saving additional information to memory selected from a group consisting of time, date, lighting conditions, display brightness, pupil size, whether the user is wearing corrective lenses at the time of recording and a combination of the foregoing.

7. The computer implemented method as claimed in claim 6, further comprising recording status as to whether the corrective lenses are worn when the optokinetic stimulus is viewed and transmitting the status as to whether corrective lenses are a worn to the health care practitioner.

8. The computer implemented method as claimed in claim 1, further comprising analyzing a captured image to determine a pupil size; and optionally, transmitting information of the pupil size to a health care practitioner.
10. The handheld digital device (10) as claimed in claim 9, wherein the processor (12) is further programmed, to present the optokinetic stimulus as a moving image of stripes, bars or checkerboards.

11. The handheld digital device as claimed in claim 9, wherein the processor (12) is further programmed, to present the optokinetic stimulus in varying directions on the display and/or wherein the processor (12) is further programmed, to present the optokinetic stimulus in a consistent direction on the display (16) and presenting instructions to the user to hold the display (16) in a desired orientation.
12. The handheld digital device as claimed in claim 9, wherein the processor (12) is further programmed, to present the optokinetic stimulus (S13) with varying width and spacing.

13. The handheld digital device as claimed in claim 9, wherein the processor (12) is further programmed to save additional information to memory (14) selected from a group consisting of time, date, lighting conditions, display brightness, pupil size, whether the user is wearing corrective lenses at the time of recording and a combination of the foregoing.

14. The handheld digital device as claimed in claim 9, wherein the processor (12) is further programmed to record status as to whether the corrective lenses are worn when the optokinetic stimulus (S13) is viewed and transmitting the status as to whether corrective lenses are a worn to the health care practitioner.

15. The handheld digital device as claimed in claim 9, wherein the processor (12) is further programmed to analyze a captured image to determine a pupil size; and optionally, transmit information of the pupil size to a health care practitioner.
